# Launch

> A Laravel 13 + React 19 + Inertia v3 starter kit with SSR, Tailwind CSS v4, shadcn (base-nova/Base UI), Laravel route files, and a typed frontend route layer. Built to be set up and extended by AI coding agents.

If you were pointed at this site to scaffold a new project, read the setup guide below. It is self-contained: follow it top to bottom and you will have a running application.

## Setup

- [Create a new project](https://launch.nckrtl.com/create.md): Complete, non-interactive instructions to create, configure, and run a new Launch project. Start here.

## Building on it

- [Conventions](https://launch.nckrtl.com/conventions.md): The rules a Launch project expects — routes in `routes/web.php`, typed frontend URLs, Base UI over Radix, design tokens, SSR constraints, commands, and the quality gates a feature must clear. Read after setup, before writing code.

## How the app is served

Read the one that matches the machine you are setting up. Both replace the environment and run steps of the main guide.

- [Laravel Herd](https://launch.nckrtl.com/herd.md): Herd serves the app itself, so `php artisan serve` and `composer dev` must not be used.
- [Orbit](https://launch.nckrtl.com/orbit.md): Orbit serves the app through a managed FrankenPHP process, so `php artisan serve` and `composer dev` must not be used.

## How long-running processes are run

Decided by the choice above: whatever serves the app owns its processes. Under Orbit they belong in Orbit (`orbit process:add`), because Orbit's runtime units inject the Vite dev-server TLS variables that a separately started process would not get.

- [Solo](https://launch.nckrtl.com/solo.md): For agents with the Solo MCP server available, and only when Orbit is not managing the project. The kit ships no `solo.yml`; writing one is part of setup.

## Source

- [launch-laravel](https://github.com/nckrtl/launch-laravel): The Laravel package the starter kit depends on.
- [launch-ui](https://github.com/nckrtl/launch-ui): The `@launch` shadcn registry and Vite config used by the starter kit.
